title: Why Cholesterol Rises in Perimenopause
description: HDL drops 12% and LDL rises 15% on average during perimenopause—learn how to protect your heart now.
perplexityQuestions: Is cholesterol testing required at 35 if I feel fine?
What cholesterol numbers are considered high at age 35?
Can you have high cholesterol with normal triglycerides?
What does it mean if my HDL is high but my LDL is also high?
competitorCoverage: Top-ranking cholesterol articles for adults usually explain the basics: what LDL, HDL, and triglycerides mean; what numbers are considered desirable or high; who should get screened and how often; and lifestyle steps like diet, exercise, weight loss, smoking cessation, and medication when needed. To compete, a new article should also cover risk-based screening, family history and genetic causes, when fasting is or isn’t needed, how to interpret mixed results (for example, high LDL with normal triglycerides), and what adults should do when their cholesterol is high but they feel fine.
